learning_outcomes.text: After successful completion of the Production module, students are able to create a CAD assembly consisting of various components.
The components already consider the requirements of later manufacturing processes.
Students can derive technical drawings for manufacturing from the component or are able to correctly interpret a technical drawing.
These drawings comply with standards and are complete in terms of manufacturability.
Students can create a selection of possible manufacturing processes for a product.
Prioritize this list of processes independently based on technical and economic aspects and identify the advantages and disadvantages of the respective processes.

syllabus_topics: Computer-aided design with common CAD systems
Creation of components as solid models using sketch and feature-based design elements
Derivation of standard-compliant drawings from components and assemblies
Systematics of manufacturing processes according to DIN 8580
Introduction to different manufacturing processes with focus on: Primary forming (casting processes, mold and core production, powder metallurgy, sintering)
Forming (solid and sheet metal forming processes, machines and tools)
Separating (processes with geometrically defined and undefined cutting edge, ablative processes, machines and tools)
Joining (selection of joining processes with detachable and non-detachable connections)

assessment_methods.method: MECB251 CAD/Rechnergest. Konstr. & Technisches Zeichnen: Written exam

assessment_rules: The module grade corresponds to the weighted grade by CP of the sub-examinations MECB251 and MECB252. The academic performance is achieved through laboratory exercises. Regular and successful participation in the laboratory exercises is a prerequisite (XP) for participation in the MECB251 exam.
